title: Settings — Workspace
description: Activate / deactivate the WP Admin Workspace — toggling the `wp_admin_workspaces_enabled` option over the REST settings surface, with a reload prompt when the value flips.

documentation.purpose: Single-checkbox DataForm over `/wp/v2/settings` — flips `wp_admin_workspaces_enabled`. Replaces the toolbar's session-scoped 'Classic wp-admin' button with a persistent setting that survives reload. Re-enabling from classic happens through the parallel Settings → WP Admin Workspaces page registered in `wp-admin-workspaces.php`, which writes the same option through the same `wp_admin_workspaces_settings` registration group.

writes.purpose: Persist the toggle. The PHP `wp_admin_workspaces_is_active()` gate reads the option on every request; the new value takes effect on the next page load.

states.renders: Centered Spinner — useEntityRecord('root','site') not yet resolved.
Notice.Root prompting Reload now after a successful save that flipped the value.

interactions.effect: `await save()`; success snackbar via `noticesStore`. If the saved value differs from the loaded one, render a Notice.Root with a Reload now action.
`window.location.reload()` — workspace_active() re-evaluates against the new option.

a11y.focus-management: Native DataForm focus order is sufficient. The Notice.Root receives focus order between the form and the Save button so the Reload action is reachable before Save.

constraints.note: Local Spinner null-guard mirrors EntityDataForm — useEntityRecord starts with record=null while resolving.

Toggling the workspace off in workspace context strands the user in classic with no workspace UI. A parallel `add_options_page` registers Settings → WP Admin Workspaces in classic so users can re-enable from there.
wp_admin_workspaces_is_active() still requires wp-content/workspace.json (or the legacy active-workspace option). The enabled flag is a veto layer, not a sufficient condition.
